reason: I'll start with the biceps side, using the muscle cells to build the muscle that bends the elbow.
expectation: I expect muscle cells to form the biceps at the front of the arm, though I don't yet know how the assembly will be shown.

alternatives.reason: I could strengthen the front bone first, but I want to build the muscle first.

effect: The cells joined into long fibres forming the biceps; the front bone still needs mineral.
reaction: The time strip made the muscle assembly clearer.
reason: I'll strengthen the front bone attachment to complete the biceps side.
expectation: I expect mineral to strengthen the radius at the attachment, though I'm not sure what the finished view will show.

alternatives.reason: I could build the triceps next, but I'd rather finish the front first.

effect: The front is complete, and the demonstration shows how the biceps pulls the radius to bend the elbow. The back still needs muscle and mineral.
reaction: Seeing the pull turn the forearm made the attachment's purpose clearer.
reason: I'll build the triceps next so the arm has the muscle that straightens the elbow.
expectation: I expect the muscle cells to form the triceps on the back, as they formed the biceps on the front.

alternatives.reason: I could add mineral first, but I want to see the muscle before strengthening its attachment.

effect: The triceps is in place behind the elbow, but the ulna still needs mineral.
reaction: The rear pull arrow makes the triceps placement clear, though the assembly feels similar to the biceps.
reason: I'll add mineral to the back attachment; it's the only available combination and should finish the triceps side.
expectation: I expect the ulna to be strengthened and a demonstration to show the triceps straightening the elbow.

effect: The back is complete. The triceps demonstration shows how pulling behind the elbow straightens it, unlike the biceps pull in front.
reaction: The matching demonstrations made the difference between the two muscles clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Completing both sides and seeing the pulls bend and straighten the elbow was most worthwhile. It connected the muscles' positions to their jobs.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps felt a little repetitive after building the biceps, even though its different placement mattered.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could produce opposite movements because of where the muscles attach.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary: the goals and pictures explained why the muscles and bone mineral belonged on each side.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how other body parts work, though I'd hope for some less repetitive choices.
